subject: botany
question_text: What is meant by homosporous and heterosporous pteridophytes? Give two examples.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.8, SAQ 4. The book prints 'Homosporus'/'heterosporus' and 'similar kindof spores' — scan and spelling noise; the standard spellings homosporous/heterosporous are used here. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The 2+2 split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Homosporous pteridophytes
lines: one kind of spore; all the spores are of
Each spore grows into a bisexual
steps.why: 'Homo' means same: the spore mother cells all give identical spores, and one spore type means one gametophyte carrying both antheridia and archegonia. Most ferns are homosporous.
common_mistakes: Writing Selaginella as a homosporous example — it is the heterosporous one.
Leaving out the examples — one of the two marks here is for them.
steps.memory_tip: Same spores → one gametophyte → both sex organs on one prothallus.
steps.margin_note: Definition plus two named genera fills the two marks.

steps.label: Heterosporous pteridophytes
lines: Two kinds of spores form from separate
steps.why: 'Hetero' means different: small microspores give male gametophytes and large megaspores give female ones, so the sexes separate at the spore stage.
common_mistakes: Writing that microspores give female gametophytes — micro goes with male, mega with female.
steps.memory_tip: Small goes with male, large with female — micro–male, mega–female.
steps.margin_note: Keep each definition next to its own examples, never as one mixed list.

insider_note: Give only the two meanings and the two examples asked for. The significance of heterospory is a separate answer and earns no mark here.
